title: Regulatory data boundary intake - Glacier Payments
summary: Initial compliance-focused intake to map data residency, logging, and key management requirements. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private options for payments product; primary constraints are PCI-adjacent controls, EU customer data residency, and legal hold for investigations.
action_items: Marcus Hale: Provide list of regulated data classes and PCI-adjacent scope (due 2026-11-09)
Samira Khan: Share Redwood security packet + regional deployment diagram (due 2026-11-04)
Jordan Lee: Draft pilot proposal for dedicated pool + benchmark plan (due 2026-11-10)
next_steps: Redwood to send security packet link and example VPC config
Customer to validate scope and confirm legal hold windows
Schedule SE-led performance benchmark for mid-November
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-02 16:00 UTC · 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Samira (Redwood SE), Marcus (Head of Compliance, Glacier), Lena (CTO), Neil (Infra), Aisha (Legal)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Um quick intros? I'll let Samira go through the technical bits after I set context.
[00:12] Marcus: Sure, Marcus here, head of compliance at Glacier Payments. We handle card-on-file tokens and PII for EU and US customers. We're trying to map what we can put on a hosted inference API versus what needs to be locked down.
[00:25] Samira: Great, hi all. I work on deployments and private infra patterns at Redwood. Today we want to understand your residency and logging constraints and then map to Hosted / Dedicated / Private options.
[00:34] Lena: Quick note, our latency SLAs for tokenization pipeline are tight, 150ms p95 for some flows, so any routing fallback that adds hops is risky.
[00:44] Neil: Also, we have an internal policy that any processing of EU customer identifiers must stay in EU regions and logs must be retained for 7 years for investigations.
[00:55] Aisha: Hi, I'm Aisha, legal. We're mainly worried about legal hold for investigations and that logs can be redacted when required. Also need to validate subprocessor flow for hosted vendors.
[01:08] Jordan: Thanks. High level question: do you expect to run all inference through Evergreen hosted models or would you prefer a Dedicated private deployment?
[01:20] Marcus: We're evaluating. Hosted appeals for speed and cost but we can't pass full card numbers or long-term PII. There's also a question about derived data — if an LLM generates anything that could be re-identifiable, that could be in scope.
[01:34] Samira: Understood. Two quick axes: data plane residency and telemetry. Hosted: we can pin region for processing but logs by default aggregate for ops; Dedicated: private GPU pools with stronger isolation and optionally VPC peering; Private: full control, air-gapped if needed.
[01:53] Lena: How narrow is "pin region" on Hosted? Like if we set EU, does it absolutely never cross an edge to US?
[02:01] Samira: Short answer: our Hosted can be region-restricted so processing and primary logs stay in the selected region. There's a nuance: control plane metadata for billing and some analytics may still flow to Redwood control plane — we can surface what fields are sent. For EU regulated flows we usually recommend Dedicated or Private to remove that uncertainty.
[02:21] Marcus: Can you point to what exactly flows to control plane? We need to show to our auditors.
[02:26] Samira: Yep, I'll send the security packet. Typically request headers, routing metadata, model version, token counts, timing metrics. We do not include full prompt text in aggregated telemetry, but raw request logs are kept for X days depending on plan. We can redact or shorten retention.
[02:42] Aisha: Legal hold — if law enforcement requests logs, can Redwood ensure logs are tamper-evident and we get chain-of-custody?
[02:51] Jordan: We have audit trails and append-only storage for logs in Dedicated/Private; for Hosted we can provide signed export bundles. Samira, is that accurate?
[03:00] Samira: Yeah, Dedicated uses customer-dedicated S3 buckets or isolated storage and can be configured to use a customer KMS so Redwood doesn't hold keys. That gives stronger chain-of-custody. We also support HSM-backed keys for escrow workflows.
[03:13] Neil: If we use customer KMS, what about model KV cache encryption and ephemeral keys on GPU? Are those persisted?
[03:21] Samira: KV cache is ephemeral in memory and may be persisted only for checkpointing during rolling upgrades. When persisted it's encrypted using the configured KMS keys for Dedicated/Private. For Hosted, persistence is minimal and managed; we can discuss retention windows.
[03:38] Marcus: Does Redwood have SOC 2 and ISO certifications? Our procurement requires SOC 2 at minimum.
[03:43] Jordan: Redwood's SOC 2 Type II is current — I'll drop the certification in the packet. We also have an ISO 27001 abstract for enterprise customers.
[03:52] Marcus: OK. On GDPR, what about data subject access requests if a customer requests deletion? Are prompts and outputs treated as personal data?
[03:59] Aisha: That's our interpretation right now—if prompts contain PII, we have to delete across backups and logs.
[04:07] Samira: We can configure request-level redaction and retention rules. For Hosted we offer shorter retention of raw requests and an opt-out to disable raw request logging. For Dedicated/Private you control S3 lifecycle and can purge per DSR. There's an operational runbook we can provide.
[04:22] Lena: One of our use cases is generating risk summaries for support agents where we feed snippets of transaction metadata — can we keep those snippets anonymized? We need to ensure model outputs can't re-derive account numbers.
[04:34] Samira: Recommend a structured transform step before sending to Redwood — tokenization or hashing of identifiers. We also have a field-level masking plugin you can deploy in the data path.
[04:45] Neil: On networking: VPC peering or private link? Which does Redwood support for Dedicated?
[04:51] Samira: We support VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink, and also express routes for on-prem. Private deployments can be entirely customer-controlled inside their VPC with no public egress.
[05:03] Marcus: What about logging retention requirements — we said 7 years earlier. That's longer than most cloud providers keep logs by default. Can we keep logs that long in Dedicated?
[05:12] Samira: Yes, Dedicated gives you retention control. We typically recommend moving long-term retention to a cold archive bucket with immutability settings. That meets legal hold and retention windows.
[05:24] Aisha: About subpoena or third-party access — if Redwood receives a legal request, do you notify us? How's that handled?
[05:31] Jordan: We notify customers unless prohibited by law. For enterprise contracts we can add notification clauses and require Redwood to contest requests that are overly broad.
[05:40] Marcus: Encryption at rest, in transit — do you support customer-managed keys (CMK) with rotation policies?
[05:46] Samira: Yes, CMKs via KMS and rotation. For Private we support HSM and on-prem KMS. We can also do key-wrapping so raw secrets never leave the customer's key boundary.
[05:58] Lena: Performance tradeoffs — if we choose Dedicated with customer KMS calls on every request will that blow latency?
[06:06] Samira: Good catch. We recommend envelope encryption: local ephemeral keys wrap with CMK to avoid a KMS RPC per request. That preserves p95 latency. We'll include recommended patterns in the benchmark worksheet.
[06:20] Neil: Any limitations around logging PII in generated outputs? Like are there controls to block outputs that contain SSNs or card numbers?
[06:28] Samira: We have an output filter pipeline that can scan and redact or block outputs. It's configurable and can run inline or as a post-process. For high-risk flows we recommend blocking and returning an error code.
[06:40] Marcus: For PCI-adjacent scope: we cannot allow raw PAN to be sent. Tokenized PANs are OK if they cannot be reversed.
[06:47] Samira: Understood. In the pilot we'll test rejection patterns and token handling.
[06:52] [06:52] Speaker 3: (mumbled) also would want to see end-to-end encryption diagrams.
[06:58] Jordan: We'll include diagrams. Also want to surface our rollback and canary policies — if a new model diverges on PII behavior you can auto-fallback to a safer variant.
[07:10] Aisha: How does Redwood certify model updates? We need evidence that model changes won't regress on privacy behavior.
[07:16] Samira: We run eval suites tied to prompt sets and quality gates. For enterprise, we can run additional privacy/regression tests in a sandbox and produce a compliance report.
[07:28] Marcus: OK this is helpful. Can you also speak to retention of transcripts for agents and support chats? Some of our logs are used for training internal models; we have to ensure training sets exclude regulated PII.
[07:40] Jordan: We don't use customer data for training by default; that's a configurable opt-in. We'll document the exact default and the opt-in flow.
[07:50] Lena: On the dedicated side, what's the SLA for availability and latency? We need a 99.95% uptime and p95 latency targets in contract.
[07:58] Samira: Dedicated customers can get SLA-level commitments. For latency we publish p95 targets per model/instance type and can include those in the SLR.
[08:08] Neil: About observability: does Redwood expose token-level cost breakdowns and per-request tracing? We need that for debugging and chargeback.
[08:16] Samira: Yes, per-request traces, token costs, and per-model dashboards in the Console. Those logs can be pushed to your SIEM via secure forwarders.
[08:28] Marcus: Quick question on backups: are there immutable snapshots for logs so that they cannot be altered? We need append-only for legal.
[08:35] Samira: Yes, we support S3 Object Lock for immutable archives when configured.
[08:40] Aisha: For contract language, we will want clear subprocessor lists and a data flow map. Also need an incident response SLA and notification timelines.
[08:50] Jordan: We'll provide a draft contract addendum and standard incident timeline — 24 hours initial notice for critical incidents, 72 hour follow-up, etc. We'll put that in the packet.
[08:59] Marcus: Anything else on residency? We may have subsidiaries in APAC that require separate tenancy. Can Redwood do multi-tenant partitioning per legal entity?
[09:10] Samira: Yes, we can partition by tenant and region, even separate Dedicated pools per legal entity. For strict isolation you'd choose Private.
[09:20] Lena: Let's talk about the pilot: what does Redwood need from us to scope a Dedicated pilot for our EU tokenization flows?
[09:26] Jordan: Ideal is a small token sample set, sample QPS profile (peak and p95), example payload shapes, and the list of sensitive fields. Marcus, can you provide that?
[09:34] Marcus: Yes, we can. I'll work with Neil to produce a redacted sample and the QPS numbers.
[09:40] Neil: We'll need a non-prod endpoint; do you provide per-customer staging for pilot?
[09:45] Samira: We can provision a pre-prod Dedicated pool or a Private staging deployment depending on your comfort. For quick proofs we sometimes use a Dedicated sandbox.
[09:54] Jordan: Next steps recap: Samira will send security packet + deployment diagrams, Jordan will send pilot proposal and pricing, Marcus will send redacted data samples and QPS. Schedule SE benchmark for week of 11/16. Any other items?
[10:07] Aisha: Please add legal to the packet distribution.
[10:10] Jordan: Absolutely. We'll cc Aisha.
[10:13] Lena: One last: do you have references from other payments customers for Dedicated?
[10:17] Jordan: We can share references and a short case study — I'll include them.
[10:21] Marcus: Perfect, thanks everyone.
[10:24] Meeting end.

Notes: transcription contains a few mis-attributions and brief crosstalk. Shared artifacts referenced: Redwood security packet (link will be provided), Dedicated pilot worksheet, benchmark plan spreadsheet.
